{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUTlVXs8AAAABYcUXAw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm--qzhCAXyY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm--q", "number": 16, "title": "Publish the WebGPU Transformer demo to GitHub Pages with GitHub Actions", "body": "## Problem

Issue #14 delivered a browser-local WebGPU inference demo, but the repository has no GitHub Pages deployment workflow and Pages is not yet enabled. A source checkout alone cannot be published as-is: `web/model/` (exported trained ONNX models) and `web/vendor/` (ONNX Runtime Web runtime assets) are generated and intentionally gitignored.

We want the actual site reachable over HTTPS on GitHub Pages, with inference computed *locally in the visitor's browser via WebGPU*, not through a Python inference server.

**Avoid a deployment/merge deadlock:** GitHub Pages publication triggered by merging to `main` cannot be verified before that merge. Implementation validation before merge and deployed-site validation after merge must be separate.

## Expected outcome

Implement a reproducible GitHub Actions build-and-deploy path for the existing static app, targeting the repository's GitHub Pages site (normally `https://takahirox.github.io/transformer-from-scratch-lab/`). Keep the existing Python CLI training, ONNX export, and browser code working. Let the implementation choose the simplest appropriate Actions workflow/packaging details under the repository's development and review guidelines.

The deploy job should generate or reuse an explicitly reproducible trained checkpoint, export its ONNX models, prepare ONNX Runtime Web runtime assets, validate and assemble only required static files into a Pages artifact, and publish it from `main`. Do not commit generated model/vendor artifacts to the source branch merely to make Pages work.

## Context and reproduction

- Browser instructions: [web/README.md](https://github.com/takahirox/transformer-from-scratch-lab/blob/main/web/README.md); static app: `web/index.html`, `web/app.js`, `web/runtime.js`.
- CLI training and export: `baseline/run.py`, `baseline/export.py`.
- Runtime preparation: `web/package.json`, `web/scripts/prepare-runtime.mjs`.
- `.gitignore` excludes `web/model/`, `web/vendor/`, and generated checkpoints.
- Related completed [Issue #14](https://github.com/takahirox/transformer-from-scratch-lab/issues/14). Its checked-in ONNX export manifest records four small models (lengths 2, 16, 32 and 64), totaling about 191 KB. GitHub Pages site size is limited; the runtime assets must also be counted.
- Repository Pages may need a one-time Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions configuration. Document any required repository-level action explicitly; do not silently assume it is already enabled.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Add a scoped GitHub Actions workflow: PR builds/checks must **not** publish; publication is triggered by a merge/push to `main` (optionally support manual dispatch). Use appropriate permissions, deployment environment and concurrency settings without unnecessary privileges.
- [ ] Build a deterministic or otherwise reproducible model/export and ONNX Runtime Web assets using the existing CLI/export scripts and pinned dependencies. Use the trained classifier, not a mock or untrained placeholder.
- [ ] Assemble a clean GitHub Pages artifact with the required `index.html`, JS/CSS, `web/model/` ONNX files + manifest/references, `web/vendor/` JS/WASM, and applicable notices. Preserve relative URLs so the app works under `/transformer-from-scratch-lab/`. No model inference server, credentials, Python virtualenv or full `node_modules/` in the deployed artifact.
- [ ] Check that all referenced build files exist, the manifest matches exported models, and packaged site size remains comfortably below the GitHub Pages 1 GB site limit. Fail the build on missing/oversized artifacts and print the actual artifact size.
- [ ] Run appropriate pre-merge tests (existing Python checks, JS build/tests, ONNX/reference checks, and a static serving/path smoke check). Reuse available browser WebGPU integration checks when feasible; do not mistake headless CI's missing GPU for a successful WebGPU run. Document skipped checks and concrete reasons.
- [ ] Document the build/deploy workflow, one-time GitHub Pages settings, local reproduction commands, expected Pages URL, browser/WebGPU requirements, and the separation of pre-merge checks from post-merge publication checks.
- [ ] Review the diff and recorded build/test evidence before merge. Keep the existing PyTorch CLI and client-only WebGPU inference behavior intact. Do not require the live Pages site to exist before merging.

## Optional validation

- End-to-end WebGPU execution on additional physical browsers/GPUs.
- Browser caching/performance, artifact download-size optimization, and repeated reproducibility runs.

## Required post-merge verification

**Required and explicitly pending until a merge to `main` triggers publication. This is not a pre-merge acceptance gate.**

1. After merging the reviewed implementation PR, inspect the **actual** GitHub Actions Pages deployment run (completion, success/failure, logs and deployed URL). Allow for the run to finish; do not infer success from a green pre-merge build.
2. On success, request the published HTTPS URL and verify that the static page loads, expected assets/manifest/ONNX/WASM are fetchable under the repository subpath, and the app is able to initialize or clearly report unsupported WebGPU. A real-WebGPU inference smoke check is preferred when an appropriate browser/device is available; otherwise record it as unverified, not passed.
3. Record the post-merge evidence with the workflow-run URL, publication URL, results, and any browser/device limitations. Track the deployment verification separately from the pre-merge approval decision.
4. **If deployment fails or the published site is broken, create a new `task`-labeled follow-up Issue** with the deployment run URL, error/symptoms, expected behavior, reproduction, and actionable pre-merge acceptance criteria. Link the merged PR and this Issue. Fix it in a separate PR. **Do not block the original merge waiting for a deployment that can only run after merge**, and do not falsely claim the deployment succeeded.
5. If repository Pages settings/permissions require a one-time human-admin change, document the exact action and track the resulting publication blocker in a follow-up Issue rather than asserting a successful deployment.

The original implementation Issue can be closed once its complete implementation and pre-merge acceptance checks pass and it is merged, while the required post-merge check remains explicitly pending until verified. A failed post-merge deployment is tracked as a **new** Issue rather than retroactively labeling the original pre-merge verification a failure.
